titulo: The folder is the context: README, AGENTS.md, and Markdown
lead: When everything is in one folder, the AI reads material that has nothing to do with your request, and you can’t tell where each sentence came from. One folder per topic, with one file for people and another for the agent, solves this before your first request.
objetivo: create the projetos/config tree and the project folder with entradas, saídas, README.md, and AGENTS.md in Markdown.
hero_alt: An open steel filing cabinet with labeled hanging folders and a laptop in the background.

aprende.t: One folder per topic, and config for what applies to all
README for people, AGENTS.md for the agent
Edit with Notepad and check with type

secoes.sub: Each drawer holds one topic. Click each part.

nos.detalhe: Brings together independent work. Each folder inside it is a context: the material for one topic. When you open the agent in a folder, it works from there.
It stays inside projetos, but outside each project. It stores what always applies, such as “I prefer short reports, with pending items at the end.” Write it once, use it everywhere.
Entradas is what the AI reads; saidas is what it produces for you to review. Keeping them separate lets you check one against the other. Don’t mix in material from another client or class here.
The agent looks for AGENTS.md on its own when it starts. It reads the rest when you point it to them: the AI doesn’t open every file in the folder on its own.

secoes.legenda: Short names, with no spaces or accents: meu-primeiro-agente, entradas, saidas.

rolagem_fim.texto: A separate folder for each topic means the AI reads less and you can tell where each sentence came from. Sketch the folder tree on paper before creating it. Take your time with the names.

texto: # at the start of a line makes a heading, ## makes a subheading, and a hyphen makes a list item. The file ends in .md and opens in any text editor.
It’s still text: readers can understand the structure even without formatting.

exemplo.texto: # Science fair  ## Materials  - cotton and a cup

texto: It explains what the project is for and how to check the result. Five sections: Purpose, Read first, Organization, How to verify, and Current status.
Don’t know a field yet? Write "to be defined". An honest blank field is better than template text no one has checked.

exemplo.texto: Every registered group appears on the final list.

texto: It tells the agent who you are, the project rules, and what’s in the folder. Claude Code and Codex read the same file, so the rules apply to both.
Start with three rules of your own. In lesson 7, it grows and gets rules you can check.

exemplo.texto: Before you finish, say what changed and how I can check it.

texto: notepad README.md opens the file in Notepad; Ctrl+S saves it. type README.md shows what was saved in cmd.
Accents displayed incorrectly in cmd, such as Ã§ instead of ç, are just a screen issue; the file is fine.

exemplo.texto: nano README.md to edit, cat README.md to view.

secoes.titulo: The folder tree and the two files
secoes.sub: Create the folders in cmd and paste the templates into Notepad. Replace what’s inside < >.

blocos.conteudo:
cd %USERPROFILE%\projetos
mkdir config
cd meu-primeiro-agente
mkdir entradas
mkdir saidas
dir /b

# My first agent

## Purpose
<what this project produces, in one sentence>

## Read first
1. AGENTS.md
2. ../config/decisoes.md
3. ../config/memoria.md

## Organization
- entradas: what the AI reads
- saidas: what it produces for me to review

## How to verify
<how someone can check that the result is correct>

## Current status
To be defined.

# Who I am
<your name, your profession, who you work for>

# Rules for this project
- Write in English, using short sentences.
- Work only inside this folder. Don’t delete files without asking.
- Before you finish, say what changed and how I can check it.

# What’s here
- entradas/: material you can read
- saidas/: where you deliver drafts

notepad README.md
notepad AGENTS.md
type AGENTS.md

abas.html:
C:\Users\ana\projetos
├─ config
└─ meu-primeiro-agente
   ├─ AGENTS.md
   ├─ README.md
   ├─ entradas
   └─ saidas

Notepad asks if you want to create the new file: answer Yes. Save with Ctrl+S and close it.

• File becomes AGENTS.md.txt: in Notepad, under File type, choose "All files", or create it with notepad AGENTS.md in cmd.
  • Everything in the Documents folder: the agent reads evidence, contracts, and notes that have nothing to do with the task.
  • Repeat the preference in every project: keep it just once, in config.

exercicios.titulo: E5 · The tree and the README
exercicios.texto: Draw the tree on paper, create config, entradas, and saidas in cmd, and write the README with the five sections.
exercicios.pronto: dir /b shows entradas, saidas, and README.md, and each README section has real information or says "to be defined".

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: You want to save "I prefer short reports, with open items at the end." Where does that note belong?
opcoes: In the config folder, outside the projects.
In entradas, for the AI to read.
perguntas.explica: A preference that applies to all projects belongs in config, in one place. Repeating it in each project creates conflicting versions.

perguntas.p: What’s the difference between README.md and AGENTS.md?
opcoes: The README is for people; AGENTS.md gives the agent work instructions.
The README is only for Codex.
perguntas.explica: Each one has a reader. The README explains the project to newcomers; AGENTS.md tells the agent how to work on it.

perguntas.p: You asked for a summary of the science fair, but a report card note showed up in the middle. What’s the likely cause?
opcoes: The folder mixed topics, and the report card note was in there too.
perguntas.explica: A folder with several topics creates noise. One folder per context helps the AI read only the material for the task.
